+# Why the first positive grade changes by about tenfold
+
+The speedup is a real first-use runtime effect, dominated by Emscripten's generated
+JavaScript filesystem error path. It is not evidence that algebra or warmed
+STACK grading becomes ten times faster.
+
+The `ecl-oz` control compiles generated Maxima C at `-O2`, but its delivered
+`maxima.js` contains the assertions-enabled `ErrnoError` class: it extends
+JavaScript `Error`, calls `super(runtimeInitialized ? strError(errno) : '')`,
+and searches `ERRNO_CODES` for the symbolic code. The candidate's admitted
+`maxima.js` instead contains:
+
+```js
+ErrnoError:class{name="ErrnoError";constructor(errno){this.errno=errno}}
+```
+
+This is an ordinary compiler output difference. `EMCC_CFLAGS=-Oz` reaches the
+final Maxima Emscripten link as well as compilation. At the pinned Emscripten
+commit, [optimized links default ASSERTIONS to zero](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/b7dc6e5747465580df5984e723b9d1f10d8e804b/tools/link.py#L695),
+and [`libfs.js` selects these two constructor forms with ASSERTIONS](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/b7dc6e5747465580df5984e723b9d1f10d8e804b/src/lib/libfs.js#L63).
+The profile therefore includes optimized JS glue and the usual optimized-link
+diagnostic defaults, alongside the generated-C optimization change. It is not
+a change confined to the mathematical C routines.
+
+A separate, calibrated [CPU capture](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/actions/runs/40171592095)
+recorded three cold and three reload first grades for each profile. In all six
+control samples, the `ErrnoError` leaf accounts for about 2.05–2.10 seconds of
+an instrumented 2.40–2.46-second first grade. In the candidate it is below the
+retained top-80 leaf frames (less than 0.6 ms in each sample); those grades take
+0.26–0.32 seconds under profiling. Most of the large first-grade difference is
+thus located in that assertions-only error-construction path. This does not
+separate the costs of message resolution, Error construction and symbolic-code
+lookup; it does not claim that stack capture alone explains the gap.
+
+The separate [LOAD/V8 diagnostic](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/actions/runs/40169523214)
+passed all 12 complete source-runtime samples. Both profiles load `genut.mac`
+during the first positive grade: roughly 0.10–0.16 seconds in the control and
+0.03 seconds in the candidate. V8 baseline-tier Wasm compilation during that grade is
+about 2.4–2.6 ms on cold loads, and absent on reloads, for both profiles. An
+O2-only lazy Wasm module load or compilation pause does not explain the gap.
+
+The profiler was enabled only around the first positive grade, after the same
+first logical check. Clock synchronization is independently checked against
+Chrome's `Performance.Timestamp`. Profile chunks are associated by process and
+profile ID, since their emitting thread differs from the sampled thread. The
+waiting parent `assess` frame and idle main thread are not added to CAS execution.
+These sampled wall weights are diagnostic, not additive CPU-time measurements.
+The initial full-session CPU capture lacked a retained clock marker and was
+excluded from phase attribution.

+# Source validation failure: collector-invisible pointers
+
+Date: 25 October 2026. Diagnostic evidence for the blocker described in
+`../VALIDATION-INVESTIGATION.md`. Raw results: `stress-results.json`.
+
+## Confirmed
+
+- **The failure is a garbage-collector use-after-free in the Wasm runtime.**
+  Raising Boehm GC frequency with `GC_FREE_SPACE_DIVISOR=1000` makes a local
+  cold build of the candidate fail the exact captured validation ([1,1]
+  against [2,2]) in 11 of 750 iterations (three runs), at the same step as the
+  CI failures: inside `stack_validate`, after the `ATList_wrongentries` note.
+  The errors are corrupted heap structure, not one fixed Lisp bug: `CAR` of
+  `SUBR`, of `#\,`, of `$EX`, of `1`; `BOUNDP` of `(MLIST SIMP)` and of a
+  source-located `MCOND` form header; once an ordinary-looking Maxima error,
+  `assignment: cannot assign to (false)`.
+- **The cause is Binaryen's spill pass, not STACK, Maxima, the PythonChecker or
+  the error boundary.** ECL configures every target link with
+  `BINARYEN_EXTRA_PASSES=--spill-pointers`, the only way pointers held in Wasm
+  locals become visible to Boehm GC on Emscripten (bdwgc scans neither static
+  data, `DATASTART == DATAEND`, nor Wasm locals). In the exact pinned Binaryen
+  (`version_123-168-g8c82b6884`), `SpillPointers` spills only pointer locals
+  live after a call. A call result waiting on the Wasm value stack as an
+  earlier operand of an enclosing call, `g(f(), h())`, is never spilled; a
+  collection inside `h()` can free `f()`'s result. Post-processing the same
+  built modules with `--flatten` before `--spill-pointers` (flattening moves
+  every such value into a local) removed every failure: 0 of 600 iterations
+  with a comparable collection count (6,483 versus 3,715 per 300). Only the
+  post-processed modules were fetched during that run.
+- **Maxima's own interrupt finalizer is not the cause.** The Wasm port re-arms
+  a finalizer on every collection (`ecl-port.lisp`, `init-cl.lisp`). Disabling
+  the re-arm still failed 5 of 300. Native ECL with threads disabled at the
+  same pins ran the program 3,000 times under heavy collection (6,362
+  finalizer runs) without failure, with and without the finalizer.
+- **Production `ecl-oz` did not fail on this path**: 0 of 1,200 iterations
+  and about 17,000 collections (divisors 1000 and 5000). It differs from the
+  candidate only in Maxima's generated C (`-O2` instead of `-Oz`), so the
+  exposed call sites on this path come from Maxima compiled at `-Oz`.
+- **The previous catch-all converted heap corruption into learner-invalid.**
+  It concealed the fault but did not cause it.
+
+## Why passing reruns were not evidence
+
+ECL's `get-internal-real-time` measures microseconds since start; Maxima reads
+it around every toplevel input. On wasm32 the value exceeds a fixnum after
+about 537 seconds and is allocated as a bignum, so wall time changes allocation
+and therefore when collections happen. Identical CAS histories can still differ
+in collection points. Collections forced between calls, as in the previous
+stress runs, never meet a pointer in flight.
+
+## Hypotheses, not established
+
+- That `-Oz` exposes more value-stack temporaries than `-O2` is consistent with
+  the profiles' results but was not measured by static counting.
+- Production `ecl-oz` uses the same incomplete spill pass for its `-Oz` ECL
+  core and `-O2` Maxima code. No failure was observed; a latent hazard on
+  other paths is not excluded.
+
+## Repair
+
+The candidate profile selects the complete pass list with `gcSpillPasses`
+(`flatten,spill-pointers,simplify-locals-notee-nostructure,vacuum,
+coalesce-locals,reorder-locals`). It reaches every Emscripten invocation through
+the existing profile-injected `EMCC_CFLAGS`, after upstream ECL's own setting,
+so upstream configure is unchanged. Compiler evidence requires, for every
+delivered target, an executed `wasm-opt` with this exact contiguous sequence
+after the optimization passes and no other spill pass. The simplification
+passes after spilling only reduce local counts (V8 rejects a flattened function
+with more than 50,000 locals); spill stores are memory writes placed before each
+call and are not removed or reordered.
+
+Independently, validation now distinguishes learner-domain errors (Maxima errors
+and Lisp arithmetic errors, such as 1/0, stay invalid without restarting) from
+internal Lisp faults, which fail the request so the session's existing
+poison/restart path discards the worker. This boundary cannot detect every
+corruption (one surfaced as an ordinary Maxima error); the pass list is the
+repair.
+
+## Regressions
+
+- `runtime/build/test-compiler-evidence.py` and
+  `runtime/precompiled/test-stack-compiler-evidence.py`: plain, reordered,
+  incomplete, re-optimized or duplicated spill passes are rejected per target.
+- `scripts/milestone-three/test-validation-boundary.py`: real native Maxima
+  (packaged and same-source ECL) keeps 1/0 invalid and fails a Lisp type error
+  as an internal fault.
+- `scripts/milestone-three/gc-stress.mjs`: the built Wasm runtime replays the
+  exact validation 400 times and all 316 captured programs once under
+  `GC_FREE_SPACE_DIVISOR=1000`, in both the compiled and source-loaded phases;
+  `runtime/build/stack_acceptance.py` requires zero deviations. On the unfixed
+  candidate the harness failed at iteration 225 of 300; on the post-processed
+  build it passed 300 of 300.

+# Binaryen `--spill-pointers` misses pointers on the Wasm value stack
+
+Boehm GC on Emscripten cannot scan Wasm locals or the Wasm value stack. Code
+that relies on conservative collection, such as ECL and therefore Maxima on
+Wasm, links with `-sBINARYEN_EXTRA_PASSES=--spill-pointers` so that pointers
+are stored to the shadow stack the collector scans. This fixture shows that the
+pass leaves one case unprotected: a call result that waits on the value stack
+as an earlier operand of an enclosing call. A collection in the nested call can
+free it. Running `--flatten` immediately before `--spill-pointers` removes the
+loss.
+
+The fixture is standalone: one C file, an unmodified bdwgc, and Node from the
+SDK. It does not use ECL, Maxima or this repository's runtime.
+
+## Tested versions
+
+| Component | Versions |
+|---|---|
+| Emscripten SDK | 4.0.10 (`62a853cd`, Binaryen `version_123-168`), 6.0.13 (`35659964`, Binaryen `version_133-96`) |
+| bdwgc | 8.2.8 bundled in the ECL Emscripten fork at `e4bdb2e5`, `src/bdwgc`; upstream 8.2.12 (`4fab5386`) |
+| Optimization | `-O0`, `-O2`, `-Oz` |
+
+The collector is built single-file from `extra/gc.c` with default settings.
+
+## Observed behavior
+
+Each case runs 2,000 rounds; each round forces one full collection.
+Results were the same for both SDKs and both collector versions:
+
+| Optimization | Plain `--spill-pointers` | `--flatten,--spill-pointers` |
+|---|---|---|
+| `-O0` | 0 lost | 0 lost |
+| `-O2` | 2,000 lost | 0 lost |
+| `-Oz` | 1,999 lost | 0 lost |
+
+Two further observations, recorded but not used as controls:
+
+- With Emscripten 6.0.13, `--spill-pointers` fails to build a module without a
+  name section: `Fatal: getStackSpace: failed to find the stack pointer`. The
+  fixture therefore adds `--profiling-funcs`. Emscripten 4.0.10 builds either way.
+- Without any spill pass, `-O2` and `-Oz` lost 1 object in 2,000. This retention
+  is not explained here; the fixture asserts only the plain-spill and flattened
+  outcomes.
+
+## Mechanism
+
+`main` evaluates `intact(make(id), churn(id), id)` through function pointers,
+so Binaryen cannot inline the calls. In the optimized plain-spill build, the
+disassembly (`O2-spill-names.wat`, here from SDK 4.0.10 with ECL's bdwgc) shows `make()`'s result set into a temporary
+local that is never stored to the shadow stack before `churn()` collects:
+
+```wat
+(local.set $7 (call_indirect (type $1) (local.get $13) (local.get $14)))   ;; make(id)
+... spill stores of $0, $2, $3, $4 only ...
+(local.set $8 (call_indirect (type $1) (local.get $11) (local.get $12)))   ;; churn(id)
+(call_indirect (type $5) (local.get $7) (local.get $8) ...)                ;; intact(...)
+```
+
+In `SpillPointers.cpp`, liveness is computed over the function's existing
+locals. A call result used directly as an operand of a later call is not a
+local, so it is not spilled. When the pass rewrites a call, it moves that call's
+operands into new temporary locals; those temporaries are not spilled either.
+The pass logic is unchanged between `version_123` and Binaryen `main` of
+2026-10-23. `--flatten` turns every such value into a local before liveness is
+computed.
+
+## Reproducer
+
+Requirements: Linux, Python 3, Git; the SDK supplies clang, Binaryen and Node.
+
+```sh
+git clone https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk.git
+emsdk/emsdk install 6.0.13 && emsdk/emsdk activate 6.0.13
+git clone https://github.com/ivmai/bdwgc.git && git -C bdwgc checkout v8.2.12
+python3 runtime/diagnostics/spill-pointers/run.py --emsdk "$PWD/emsdk" \
+  --gc "$PWD/bdwgc" --output "$PWD/spill-evidence"
+```
+
+The driver writes `report.json` with every build and run command, its exit code
+and output, and fails unless the flattened builds lose nothing, `-O0` plain
+spilling loses nothing, and optimized plain spilling loses objects (the
+negative controls). The [independent diagnostic CI run](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/actions/runs/40231542637) runs both SDKs against both collectors on the diagnostic branch. The production build does not depend on that experiment workflow.
+
+## Limits
+
+- The fixture forces the pattern with indirect calls and a collection in every
+  round. It shows that the pass can miss such a value, not how often real code
+  produces this pattern.
+- `--flatten` increases local counts; large modules then need local
+  simplification (for example `--simplify-locals-notee-nostructure --vacuum
+  --coalesce-locals --reorder-locals`) to stay below V8's limit of 50,000 locals
+  per function. Those passes are not needed for this small fixture.

+  `measurements/2026-10-25-maxima-oz-selection/gc-root-cause/` on branch
+  `runtime/promote-maxima-oz`) is consistent with this mechanism; this fixture
+  is the independent demonstration.

+
+def run(argv, env, cwd):
+    process = subprocess.run(argv, env=env, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)

+              'gc': str(args.gc), 'rounds': args.rounds, 'cases': [], 'failures': []}
+    for names in ('names', 'stripped'):
+        for opt in ('-O0', '-O2', '-Oz'):
+            for kind, passes in PASSES.items():
+                if names == 'stripped' and kind != 'spill':
+                    continue
+                name = f'{opt[1:]}-{kind}-{names}'
+                argv = ['emcc', opt, '-I', str(args.gc / 'include'), str(HERE / 'spill-gap.c'), str(args.gc / 'extra/gc.c'),
+                        '-sSTACK_SIZE=33554432', '-sALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH', '-o', name + '.js']

+                    argv.insert(2, '--profiling-funcs')
+                if passes:

+                case = {'name': name, 'optimization': opt, 'passes': kind, 'names': names, 'build': run(argv, env, args.output)}
+                if case['build']['exitCode'] == 0:

+    raise SystemExit(0 if report['passed'] else 1)

+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3

+"""Run engine-generated native validation programs in real native Maxima.
+
+Learner domain errors (1/0) must stay invalid inside a working program. Any
+other Lisp error inside STACK validation must fail the whole program with the
+engine's internal-fault message, so the Wasm session is poisoned and restarted
+instead of reporting learner-invalid. The fault is raised by a deliberately
+admitted Lisp call; production admission never permits '?'.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import os
+import importlib.util
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import tempfile

+reference = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+spec.loader.exec_module(reference)
+
+GENERATE = r"""
+import {readFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
+import vm from 'node:vm';
+import {webcrypto} from 'node:crypto';
+const scope = {NativeInput:{AdmissionError:class extends Error {},admit:raw => ({raw,source:raw})}};
+vm.runInContext(await readFile(process.argv[1],'utf8'),vm.createContext({self:scope,TextEncoder,crypto:webcrypto}));
+const question = {name:'Boundary',variables:'startx:-2;',native:{schema:1,id:'boundary',locals:['startx'],tokens:[]},
+  inputs:[{name:'ans',type:'algebraic',checkanswertype:true,requirelowestterms:false}],prts:[]};
+const variant = {seed:1,env:{startx:'-2'},teachers:{ans:{source:'[2,2]'}}};
+const engine = new scope.NativeStackEngine({session:{evaluate(){throw new Error('unused');}}});
+const program = (raw,type='algebraic') => engine.validationExpression(
+  {...question,inputs:[{...question.inputs[0],type}]},variant,{ans:{raw,source:raw}});
+// STACK's validator itself reports algebraic 1/0. The numerical check runs
+// after it, so its Maxima error unwinds to the engine's classified boundary.
+console.log(JSON.stringify({fault:scope.NativeStackEngine.INTERNAL_FAULT,
+  programs:{list:program('[1,1]'),domain:program('1/0'),numericDomain:program('1/0','numerical'),
+    internal:program('?car(1)'),after:program('[1,1]')}}));
+"""
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--stack-source", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--maxima", default="maxima")
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    executable = shutil.which(args.maxima)
+    assert executable, "Native Maxima executable unavailable: " + args.maxima
+    generated = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(
+        ["node", "--input-type=module", "-e", GENERATE, str(ROOT / "prototype/native/engine.js")], text=True))
+    names = list(generated["programs"])
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="validation-boundary-") as directory:
+        home = Path(directory)
+        lines = reference.make_batch(args.stack_source.resolve(), home, []).splitlines()
+        assert lines[-2:] == ['m3_emit("CTMNATIVE-END|0")$', "quit()$"]
+        lines = lines[:-2]
+        for index, name in enumerate(names):
+            marker = reference.literal(f"CTMNATIVE-REFERENCE|{index}|")
+            # Same outer envelope as MaximaSession.evaluate, retaining the message.
+            lines.append('block([%ERR:["stack_map"],%NOTES:["stack_map"],%FEEDBACK:["stack_map"],%stmt:"ctm-native",_r],'
+                         "_r:errcatch(" + generated["programs"][name] + "),"
+                         "if _r=[] then m3_emit(sconcat(" + marker + ",stackjson_stringify([false,errormsgtostring()]))) "
+                         "else m3_emit(sconcat(" + marker + ",stackjson_stringify([true,first(_r)]))))$")
+        lines += [f'm3_emit("CTMNATIVE-END|{len(names)}")$', "quit()$"]
+        batch = home / "boundary.mac"
+        batch.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        process = subprocess.run([executable, "--very-quiet", f"--batch={batch}"],
+                                 capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900, check=False)
+    output = process.stdout + process.stderr

+    valid = {"valid": True, "latex": "\\left[ 1 , 1 \\right] ", "feedback": "", "source": "[1,1]"}
+    assert observed["list"] == [True, {"ans": valid}], observed["list"]
+    invalid = {"valid": False, "latex": "", "feedback": "Native STACK could not evaluate this expression", "source": ""}
+    domain = observed["domain"]
+    assert domain[0] is True and domain[1]["ans"]["valid"] is False and domain[1]["ans"]["feedback"].endswith(invalid["feedback"]), domain
+    assert observed["numericDomain"] == [True, {"ans": invalid}], observed["numericDomain"]
+    assert observed["internal"][0] is False and observed["internal"][1].startswith(generated["fault"]), observed["internal"]
+    assert observed["after"] == observed["list"], "A caught internal fault must not alter later validation"
+    report = {"schema": 1, "passed": True,
+              "sourceRevision": os.environ.get("GITHUB_SHA") or subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=ROOT, text=True).strip(),
+              "stackRevision": reference.STACK_SHA,

+              "observed": observed,
+              "scope": "Engine-generated validation programs in one native Maxima process with pinned STACK source. "
+                       "Domain error stays learner-invalid; a Lisp error fails the program as an internal fault."}
+    if args.output:
+        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    print(json.dumps({"passed": True, "maxima": report["maxima"], "internal": observed["internal"][1][:160]}))
+    return 0
+

+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
